name: OTDC Panthanivas Harishankar Restaurant
signature_dish: Odia thali lunch and dinner at the government tourist lodge
why_it_matters: The OTDC Panthanivas at Harishankar, inaugurated on 18 May 2010, is the only proper sit-down dining option at this remote twin-temple pilgrimage site on the Balangir side of the Gandhamardan Hills. Run by the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation, its restaurant serves lunch and dinner to the large number of pilgrims and picnickers — visitors consistently report good, simple meals and helpful staff.
insider_tip: Breakfast is limited here, so carry your own morning food; lunch and dinner are the reliable meals. It is best to inform the kitchen ahead, as this is a quiet government lodge that cooks to demand rather than holding a buffet. Combine with the temple-prasad option for the full pilgrim experience.
signature_address: OTDC Panthanivas, Harishankar, Gandhamardan Hills, Balangir district, Odisha 767066

name: Harishankar Temple Prasad
signature_dish: Temple prasad served in the temple veranda
why_it_matters: Harishankar Temple, dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu and set beside a hill spring on the Gandhamardan slopes, serves prasad to pilgrims directly in its veranda. It is documented as available from roughly 12 to 4pm at a nominal rate of around ₹45 with no prior booking — the simplest, most authentic meal at this remote pilgrim site.
insider_tip: Prasad service is midday only — plan darshan and lunch together between noon and 4pm. Pay before you eat; no booking needed. For breakfast or dinner, the OTDC Panthanivas restaurant nearby is the fallback.
signature_address: Harishankar Temple, Gandhamardan Hills, Balangir district, Odisha 767066

name: Nrusinghanath Temple Prasad
signature_dish: Temple prasad ordered at the temple office
why_it_matters: Nrusinghanath Temple sits at the foot of the Gandhamardan Hills near Paikmal in Bargarh district — the Bargarh-side counterpart to Harishankar. It is a popular pilgrim and picnic spot, and the temple office serves prasad to visitors. With no proper restaurant at the site itself, the temple prasad is the honest on-site meal option.
insider_tip: Order prasad at the temple office on arrival. The site is a known picnic spot, so many visitors carry their own food; the nearest market meals are in Paikmal and Padmapur towns. Combine Nrusinghanath with Harishankar on the same Gandhamardan circuit, though they are reached from different sides of the hills.
signature_address: Sri Sri Nrusinghanath Temple, near Paikmal, Bargarh district, Odisha 768040
